fallback_basis: No soldier of the garrison can be drawn as a known person. The only person this project records at Chicago in August 1812 is John Kinzie the elder, a silversmith and trader, and no man of Heald's company has a record of his own, though the company's muster-roll survives. So this figure stands for none of them by name and adds no one to the people of the town.

provenance.basis: An anonymous private of Captain Nathan Heald's company of the First Regiment of Infantry, the garrison of the first Fort Dearborn, whose muster-roll Quaife printed in 1913. He stands at ease on the parade, the open square of Whistler's plan of the fort (1808), a few metres west of the way from the main gate to the flagstaff, facing the gate, on the afternoon of 14 August 1812. Nothing of that day is acted out: not the order to leave, the council, the giving out of the goods, the march or the attack. His blue coat faced red, black leather stock, white crossbelts, white linen overalls, half gaiters and tall felt cap with a white feather follow the issue the 1802 act lists and the uniform change of 1813 read backwards. Where he stands, his face, his build and his age are reconstructed; his age, about 26, is a seeded draw kept near the young private the dress was made for.
provenance.replaceable_by: A person record for a named soldier of Heald's company in the 1812 people layer, who would stand in this place instead; his place on the parade and his standing have no documentary claim.
